overview: re;Flux is a reactive TypeScript animation library. The core remains headless; rendering adapters are optional. The capabilities below distinguish implemented APIs from remaining hardening and integration work.

features.title: First-class gesture physics
features.summary: Turn pointer input into typed motion streams, with drag inertia and following motion as composable RxJS operators.
features.problem: Drag implementations often mix event listeners, velocity calculations, mutable state, and cleanup in one component.
features.approach: Keep DOM event normalization optional and put the physics in pure operators that emit position, velocity, and timestamps.
criteria: Time-based physics behaves consistently across frame rates.
Pointer cancellation and unsubscription clean up all listeners.
Core operators emit data and never write to the DOM.

features.title: Real-time stream smoothing
features.summary: Smooth irregular WebSocket, SSE, telemetry, and GPS samples with fixed-latency buffering or cadence-adaptive transition duration.
features.problem: Rendering each arriving network sample immediately makes motion jump when packet timing varies.
features.approach: Sample timestamped values against the shared frame clock. smoothStream uses fixed display latency; adaptiveTween estimates input cadence and adjusts the duration between successive targets. Neither operator predicts future data.
criteria: Frame-aligned interpolation and bounded memory are implemented.
Duplicate/out-of-order, stale, invalid and finite-source behavior have unit tests.
adaptiveTween adapts transition duration to cadence; prediction remains intentionally separate.

features.title: Seamless interruption and retargeting
features.summary: Switch animation targets without snapping back to the original start value or discarding momentum.
features.problem: Interrupting a tween can cause visual jumps or force applications to implement cancellation and continuity manually.
features.approach: Carry the current value, velocity, and timestamp into the next target transition. The operator owns one motion per subscription and waits for the last target to settle after source completion.
criteria: Retargeting starts from the latest sampled value and velocity.
Source completion waits for the final target to settle; unsubscribe cancels work.
Rapid target changes and stream errors remain leak-free.

features.title: Frame coordinator
features.summary: Coalesce library work into one frame-aligned coordinator with explicit read and write phases.
features.problem: Independent updates can repeat work or interleave layout reads and DOM writes, causing avoidable layout thrashing.
features.approach: Reuse RxJS animationFrameScheduler where suitable and add only the library-specific batching coordinator we need.
criteria: One pending coordinator RAF while work is queued.
A shared timestamp is passed to every task in a frame.
Read/write ordering and cancellation semantics are deterministic.

features.status: DOM / SVG / Canvas / Three.js adapters implemented
features.title: Headless rendering adapters
features.summary: Connect the same motion streams to DOM, SVG, Canvas, Three.js, or framework state without coupling the core to them.
features.problem: DOM-first engines make it harder to reuse the same motion logic in Canvas, WebGL, or server-side contexts.
features.approach: Keep the core headless and publish thin opt-in adapters that own their subscriptions and restore original target state on teardown.
criteria: DOM/SVG adapters restore original styles or attributes on unsubscribe.
Canvas drawing is coalesced through the shared frame write phase.
The Three.js adapter uses structural types and adds no Three.js dependency to the core.

features.title: Typed keyframes and DOM targeting
features.summary: Define explicit start/end values, keyframes, per-property timing, and per-target frames while keeping the DOM adapter optional.
features.problem: Low-level progress controls are flexible but verbose for common UI tasks, while selector helpers should not force DOM dependencies into the core.
features.approach: Use one property configuration that accepts from/to, values, keyframes, or a target-aware factory. The factory receives the resolved element, index, and total once at animation creation.
criteria: Supports selector strings, individual elements, and iterable targets.
Supports shorthand frames, explicit from/to, normalized keyframes, and target-aware value factories.
Global and property timing settings have documented precedence and validation.
Target factories run once per target at creation, not on animation frames.
DOM adapter remains optional and existing public imports remain stable.

principles.title: Observable-first
principles.text: Motion, time, and velocity are values in streams—not hidden mutable globals.

principles.title: Headless by default
principles.text: Rendering is an adapter concern. Core logic produces values and timestamps.

principles.title: Deterministic tests
principles.text: Clock-dependent behavior must be testable with an injected or virtual clock.

principles.title: Honest performance
principles.text: Frame alignment reduces redundant work, but cannot guarantee 60 or 120 FPS under browser throttling.

implementationHeading: Stabilize timeline contracts, benchmark hot paths, then expand the API.
implementationSummary: Timeline duration lookup and pre-start resets are now optimized, nested timelines have explicit single-parent ownership, and frame-work timing is collected only while metrics are observed. Remaining work focuses on browser integration, stress coverage, and consumer package smoke tests.

implementationOrder.title: Browser integration coverage
implementationOrder.detail: Test pointer capture and cancellation, style restoration, layout effects, and adapter cleanup in a real browser.

implementationOrder.title: Performance baselines and regression checks
implementationOrder.detail: Track duration lookup, timeline seeking and frame-coordinator overhead with and without metrics observers; compare results across changes.

implementationOrder.title: Stress and property tests
implementationOrder.detail: Exercise irregular streams, rapid retargeting, re-entrant frame scheduling, and subscription cleanup.

implementationOrder.title: Consumer package smoke tests
implementationOrder.detail: Install the produced tarball in a clean fixture and import every documented public entry point.

implementationOrder.title: Complete adapter examples
implementationOrder.detail: Add realistic examples for SVG path morphing, Canvas lifecycle, and structural Three.js integration.
